text:
Fraser Minten came to Boston from Toronto as a prospect in a deadline trade, and at 22 he is now a full-time middle-six forward playing 16 and a half minutes a night. Twelve points in 18 games, six goals, and some big nights early (a goal and an assist against San Jose, 20 minutes in Los Angeles).

Enjoy the start but discount it. He has six goals on 4.17 expected and is shooting 17%, and the Bruins have scored ten more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, the largest on-ice luck figure in this batch. His actual 5v5 shot share is under water (48% of attempts). Our numbers expect his scoring to drift back toward the middle of his range.

What looks durable is how he gets into the zone. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 60% of his entries last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.1 wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense. He is a real NHL player. He just isn't a 17% shooter.
headline: Minten's goals are running ahead of the chances
